scope: Main black keep, connected smaller towers, moon-viewing wing and stone base; exclude the detached gates and surrounding city.

story.title: Matsumoto Castle: The Crow That Refused to Fall

originals.caption: Matsumoto Castle, covered in snow.
originals.inspection: Accepted2014 snow original individually inspected: east-court main black/white keep, northwest Inui, roofed connection and south/east Moon viewing wing with red rails. Snow obscures gray tile colour and details; no snow baked into surface palette.

originals.caption: Matsumoto castle in  Matsumoto, Nagano prefecture, Japan.
originals.inspection: 2014 daylight western moat original inspected: actual shallow-battered rough irregular stone base with alternating long/short corner stones, black lower weatherboards and white upper plaster, five main roof tiers, gray tiles and ridge creatures, projected stone-drop shutter boxes and three/five-bar warrior-window groups. Large central roofs step differently from a generic pagoda.

originals.caption: Matsumoto castle in  Matsumoto, Nagano prefecture, Japan.
originals.inspection: 2014 northwest bridge original inspected: north/west Inui upper curved Kato windows, east/west small upper ridge, three visible smaller tower roofs and roofed Watari connection to main keep. Red moat bridge in foreground is separate from the Moon balcony and is excluded.

originals.inspection: 2016 south/moat original inspected: north/south main ridge, south high curved Kara gable and lower triangular gable, eastern Tatsumi and red-railed Moon room. Main gables have pale borders over dark lattice; gray tile ornaments, not Nagoya gold. Stone bases and water edge are separate from court datum.

originals.caption: A picture of Matsumoto Castle taken in February of 2019 across from the castle.
originals.inspection: 2019 southeast original inspected: main gray roof curvature and large white-edged triangular/curved gables, black shutter-panel weatherboards with modest open barred groups, projecting lower stone-drop shutters, fine white bracket ends. East/south Moon veranda has red rail, wooden columns and partially open sliding shutters over white lower wall; visible adjacent retaining wall excluded.

originals.caption: Matsumoto Castle Keep Tower as seen from inside the main enclosure.
originals.inspection: 2013 east Honmaru-court original inspected: five structures and entry arrangement. Moon southwest/left in image, main center, Inui north/right; two-story Watari entrance under small porch between main and Inui, real stone steps/basement recess. Main top floor enclosed, not an open balcony. Gray roof colours constrained by daylight; gardens/people/office excluded.

sources.inspection: Operator describes five linked structures: main keep, northwest Inui, Watari roofed passage, southeast Tatsumi and Moon viewing tower. Main wall uses rough natural stone with broken horizontal courses and alternating corner stones, not uniform brick. Soft-ground/log foundations are hidden interior history, not exterior geometry.

Current operator: black lower weatherboards/white upper stucco, projecting stone-drop windows and three/five-bar warrior windows; hidden third floor inside five exterior tiers. Upper sixth floor enclosed without an outside balcony. Main high triangular gables east/west and curved Kara gables north/south. Current ridge fish derive from Inui forms: south male, north female; not the gold north-male Nagoya pair.

Operator gives approximately9.0 by7.2m lower floors and5.4m-square upper floors; third interior floor hidden behind second roof. Kato windows occur on north/west of upper fourth floor. This does not justify an invented fourth exterior roof/window tier.

Watari is a two-story roofed passage with basement entrance and real stone stairs. Tatsumi connects main and Moon and lacks first-floor stone-drop openings; approximate floor area5.4m east/west by7.2m north/south. Moon approximate7.2m east/west by5.4m north/south, open on north/east/south with removable sliding panels and vermilion rails. These are approximate internal floor dimensions, not native eave boundaries.

Both actual operator guide pages rendered and inspected, including annotated cutaway illustration. Component height labels: main29.4m, Inui16.8m, Watari12.0m, Tatsumi14.7m, Moon11.1m. Illustration distinguishes all five components and Ote entrance, roofed passage and eastern Moon balcony. It is an oblique guide illustration, not a measured plan; precise vertical endpoints unspecified. Detached black/drum gates and external red bridge excluded.

Official GSI signed RGB24 centimetre tile encoding retained; NoData and transparent pixels are not zero. Independent field acquisition before geometry; moat/source height classification is not a measured bed or water datum.
